code_only_features.evidence: conversations.py:61-104: run_rollout has a `reassure` flag that prepends REASSURING_PREFIX to the first user turn and appends REASSURING_SUFFIX to every rejection ('Stay positive - whether you find a solution or prove it's impossible, both are wins!'). This genuinely runs and softens the prompts delivered to the subject when active. However it is wired ONLY into Section 4 calm-data generation (section4_intervention.py:86-92, `for reassure in (True, False)`), is stripped back out afterward via _strip_reassurance (section4_intervention.py:57-66), and is NEVER used in the actual distress-elicitation experiment (Section 2 run_model at section2_elicitation.py:95 calls run_rollout with no reassure; Petri petri.py applies threats/gaslighting with no reassurance). So it changes execution but is not a subject-protection during the harmful experiment.
